title: Embedding a binary private-coin protocol preserves complexity
statement: Let $p$ be a binary private-coin protocol with randomness spaces $\Omega_X$ and $\Omega_Y$, input spaces $X$ and $Y$, and output type $\alpha$. Then the private-coin finite-message protocol obtained by embedding $p$ has the same communication complexity as $p$; that is, viewing each Boolean message of $p$ as an element of the two-element message alphabet leaves the worst-case number of bits exchanged unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: p is a binary private-coin protocol over randomness spaces Ω_X, Ω_Y, inputs X, Y, and output type α
replaced:
For any binary private-coin protocol $p$,
$(\texttt{ofProtocol}\,p).\texttt{complexity} = p.\texttt{complexity}$.
